questions.question: How does the new cusp-unramified geometrically maximal covering compare in degree with Mazur's Shimura covering?

options.A: It is cyclic of degree 2Np, twice the Shimura degree Np
options.B: It is cyclic of degree Np/2 and factors through X1(p)

questions.rationale: The result doubles the degree of the maximal geometrically unramified cover by allowing ramification at cusps.

questions.question: What is the relation between the constructed X′₂(p) cover and the Shimura cover X₂(p)?

options.A: X′₂(p)→X₂(p) has degree two and is unramified outside cusps
options.B: X₂(p)→X′₂(p) has degree two and is étale everywhere
options.C: The two curves are disjoint degree-Np covers of X₀(p)
options.D: X′₂(p) is the unique degree-two quotient of X₁(p) ramified only at elliptic points

questions.rationale: The new map factors through the Shimura cover via a quadratic extension ramified at the cusps.
questions.evidence_quote: πp : X′2(p) → X2(p) is a degree two covering that is unramified outside cusps.

questions.question: For X₀(p) with both cusps removed, what group is LD and what quotient term does it contribute to the twisted exact sequence?

options.B: LD≅Z² with cyclotomic action, contributing Z/pZ
options.C: LD is finite of order Np and contributes zero
options.D: LD≅Q/Z with trivial action, contributing Q/Z

questions.rationale: Two rational cusp points yield a rank-one character group modulo the diagonal copy of Gm.
questions.evidence_quote:
It follows that LD = Z
with trivial GQ-action

questions.question: Which general condition makes the map Σ(f)→ΣD(f) an isomorphism in the paper's comparison of proper and cusp-open covers?

options.A: For every boundary point x, the gcd of ramification indices e(x′/x) over its preimages is 1
options.B: The cover has prime degree and is ramified at every cusp
options.C: The Jacobian has no rational torsion
options.D: The base curve has genus zero

questions.rationale: Lemma 2.4.2 states this boundary ramification-index condition makes the right vertical map injective, hence the induced kernel map surjective as well.

options.C: Take the identity cover of X₁(p)
options.D: Use a cubic cover ramified at the elliptic points

questions.question: How does the proof certify that the quadratic extension generated by √(Fh²) ramifies at the cusps rather than at ordinary points?

options.A: Fh² has odd order at each cusp and order zero elsewhere
options.B: Fh has simple zeros at every elliptic point and no cusp poles
options.C: The discriminant is supported on supersingular points
options.D: Every cusp has even valuation, forcing unramified quadratic splitting

questions.rationale: Odd valuation of the defining function at cusps forces ramification there, while no other zeros or poles occur.

questions.question: Why does the authors' main eta-product construction require a separate argument when p≡11 mod 12?

options.A: Then ℓ=1 and Γ₂(p)=Γ₁(p), so they instead build Gh from a triple h with h₁²+h₂²+h₃²≡0 mod p
options.B: Then Np is even and the Shimura cover is already ramified at elliptic points
options.C: Then no generalized Dedekind eta functions exist at level p
options.D: Then X₀(p) has more than two cusps and LD has rank two

questions.rationale: The proof says the preceding lemma assumes ℓ≠1 and changes the modular-function construction in the exceptional congruence class.

questions.question: What group-theoretic property of Γ′₂(p) establishes the degree and cyclicity of the final cover over X₀(p)?

options.B: Γ₀(p)/Γ′₂(p) is a product of two cyclic groups of order k
options.C: Γ₁(p)/Γ′₂(p) has order 2 and is noncyclic

questions.rationale: The kernel of the specified order-two character has index 2k in Γ₀(p), yielding a cyclic degree-2Np covering.
